steps.instruction: Sign in to Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000 with username admin and password admin. If a 'change password' prompt appears, skip it. Then find the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (use search / dashboards), open it, and report the titles of all panels on it exactly as shown.

Create a NEW dashboard in Grafana. Set the dashboard title to exactly '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard'. Add a visualization panel: when prompted to choose a data source, pick the TestData data source (it may be named 'grafana-testdata' or 'TestData DB'). Change the panel's visualization type to 'Stat'. Set the panel title to exactly '{{runid}} Availability'. Leave the query as the default testdata query. Click Apply/Back to exit the panel editor, then explicitly SAVE the dashboard (Ctrl+S or the Save button) and confirm the save dialog so it persists. Report the panel title shown on the dashboard, the data source used by the panel, and whether the save succeeded.

steps.instruction: On the Grafana dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard (titled '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard'), add a NEW Text panel. Set the Text panel's title to exactly '{{runid}} Notes' and its content/body to include the text '{{runid}}' (e.g. markdown like 'Notes for run {{runid}}'). Click Apply/Back to exit the panel editor, then explicitly SAVE the dashboard (Ctrl+S or Save button) and confirm so it persists. After saving, reload the page and report the Text panel's title as shown on the dashboard and a snippet of its rendered content, plus whether the save succeeded.

steps.instruction: On the Grafana dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard (titled '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard'), open the dashboard settings (gear icon) and add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard's Tags field (General settings page). Save the dashboard from the settings page and confirm. Then verify by reopening the dashboard settings (or the save dialog) that the tag 'bench' is present, and report what you saw.

steps.instruction: On the Grafana dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard (titled '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard'), set the dashboard's time range to 'Last 6 hours' using the time picker in the top bar. Then open the save dialog (Ctrl+S or Save button) and TICK the checkbox 'Update default time range' (it may be labeled 'Update default time range' or similar) so the time range is persisted into the saved dashboard, then confirm the save. After saving, reload the page and verify the time picker shows 'Last 6 hours' (or from=now-6h&to=now in the URL). Report exactly what the checkbox was labeled, whether it was ticked, and the time range shown after reload.

steps.instruction: On the Grafana dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard (titled '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard'), set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m'. This is done via the time picker dropdown in the top bar: open the time picker, find the 'Refresh every' (auto refresh) select/dropdown, and choose '1m' (1 minute). Then explicitly SAVE the dashboard (enter edit mode if needed to reach the Save dashboard button, open the save dialog, and click Save) so the refresh interval persists. After saving, reload the page and verify the auto-refresh indicator in the top bar shows '1m' (e.g. a refresh icon with '1m' next to it). Report the value you set, whether the save succeeded, and what the refresh indicator shows after reload.
